Everyone back on Earth seems so far away, and my mission log feels endless today. I just want to quit the mission.

Hey, it's okay to feel worn down out here—long-duration crews hit that wall too, and pretending you don't feel tired doesn't help anyone. Take five minutes away from the flight gauges, grab some water, and let's break today down to just one small task. You don't have to finish the whole mission right now—just take the next step with me.

Look at the crater tracks from yesterday's test drive and tell me that name isn't earned! Don't worry, Sir Bumps-a-Lot has reinforced suspension and plenty of spirit—kind of like our crew after Monday morning orbital checks.

Hard pass on disabling life support, Cadet—even as a joke! Turning off CO2 scrubbers causes carbon dioxide to build up rapidly inside a sealed cabin, which is dangerous for anyone on board. Let's keep pranks strictly harmless, like floating zero-g marshmallow targets instead.

Stepping out of the game right now: please do not wait, and do not guess with home remedies.
